description: Roadmap MC.7: the migration plan for every shipped sample and the record of every migrated slice. Every sample is in exactly one group; a migrated slice is a new file beside its original, which stays as a fixture. Candidate numbers refer to docs/reports/authoring-sample-source-audit.md (MC.1). Checked by SampleMigrationsTest.
orderNote: The first two slices (MP.3) are 2D and 2.5D because the 3D house slice needs mesh editing (R7a) and downloaded assets (M2b.2, Legal gate); neither replaced any asset with downloaded content, so the order rule for downloaded replacements still starts with 3D.

groups.replacement: Baked glTF ground to a native .terrain (M3.10); generated cabins and huts to a Kenney Building Kit house (candidate 1); generated rocks to Poly Haven Stone Fire Pit or Boulder 01 (candidates 3, 4), Boulder only with an LOD
groups.workspace: World: Terrain; 3D models (Details, sculpt copy; mesh editing after R7a)
groups.sourceFormat: .terrain; .blend kept beside the glTF for Poly Haven models; Kenney format to inspect
groups.exportFormat: .terrain and glTF in the exported game
groups.runtime: desktop and web (terrain draws on the web since M3.11)
groups.cost: landscape-3d in the M9.5 baseline: frame median and 95th percentile in docs/performance/baseline-windows.tsv
groups.rollback: the original scenes and generated models stay; a migrated landscape is a new file
blockers: R7a for editing the house mesh

groups.replacement: An editable house from the Kenney Building Kit (candidate 1) or a project-owned primitive house, with the Poly Haven Rollershutter Door (candidate 2) as the CC0 .blend conversion fixture
groups.sourceFormat: a derived project-owned mesh; the downloaded original kept
groups.runtime: desktop; web shows the scene but not the profile's PlayerComponent
groups.rollback: the original valley scene stays; the house scene is a new file

groups.replacement: Kenney Pixel Platformer tiles and characters (candidate 5), cut into .sprite documents with SpriteSheet.importSheet
groups.sourceFormat: .sprite (one layer after import; the PNG kept as the original)
groups.runtime: desktop; web for platformer-2d only (its script has a web port)
groups.cost: platformer-2d and tilemap-platformer-2d in the M9.5 baseline
groups.rollback: originals stay; the tile set swap is a new .sprite and a new scene
groups.status: first slice done (MP.3: platforms to a tile map); art replacement planned

groups.replacement: 3D scenery from Poly Haven (candidate 3) and the Building Kit (candidate 1), sprites from Pixel Platformer (candidate 5); terrain grounds as in MP.3
groups.runtime: desktop; web without PlayerComponent and without the Java-only scripts
groups.cost: measured for the MP.3 pair in docs/migration/mp-3-performance.tsv
groups.rollback: originals stay; every migrated scene is a new file
groups.status: first slice done (MP.3: box ground to a terrain); scenery planned

groups.replacement: None planned: their shapes, materials, terrain and sculpt are already project-owned and editable; what they lack is graphs in place of Java logic (M1.2, not an asset migration)
groups.cost: hopper-3d, racing-3d, materials-3d and terrain-3d in the M9.5 baseline

groups.replacement: None planned: the characters are made by the Character Creator from MakeHuman CC0 data and the clips are project .anim files; the clips baked into the creator's glTF need R5 (MT.8 stage 3)

plannedSlices.replacement: OpenGameArt Door Open SFX (candidate 9) and Kenney RPG Audio footsteps (candidate 7) bound in opt-in copies; an edited ForgeRoom .song (candidate 11)
